Paragraph:
Translation: O Krsna, maintainer of the people, I have heard by disciplic succession that those who destroy family traditions dwell always in hell.

Purport (Excerpt): Arjuna bases his argument not on his own personal experience, but on what he has heard from the authorities... One who is always engaged in sinful activities must utilize the process of ablution called the prayascitta. Without doing so, one surely will be transferred to hellish planets to undergo miserable lives as the result of sinful activities.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna invokes religious authority and scripture to validate his fears, expressing a deep terror of eternal damnation for participating in the war.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: He states that he has 'heard by disciplic succession' (from teachers and scripture) that his actions will lead straight to hell, thereby claiming a religious mandate for his refusal to fight.
Outcome/Resolution: He reinforces his emotional paralysis with the heavy weight of religious dogma and the fear of cosmic punishment.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.dogmatic Thinking: Rigid adherence to rules out of fear

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Parampara (Disciplic succession; Arjuna cites authoritative knowledge to back his claim)
Naraka (Hell; the destination for those who commit grave sins without atonement)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna uses a valid principle (learning through authoritative succession) to support an invalid conclusion. He is clinging to general religious rules meant for ordinary circumstances, failing to realize that the Supreme Authority (Krishna) is standing right in front of him, superseding general rules.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This reflects a manifestation of 'scrupulosity' (a form of obsessive-compulsive anxiety focused on moral or religious issues). Arjuna is obsessively focused on the fear of committing a sin and going to hell, using religious text to validate his intense psychological avoidance of the conflict.
